steps.text: In a medium sauce pan, mix together sugar, peanut butter, and corn syrup. Be careful not to let it burn, or it will ruin the recipe. Stir mixture until well melted. Remove pan from heat.
Combine warm peanut butter mixture with crisp rice cereal.
Grease well a 9x13 inch pan with butter or margarine. Spread mixture in pan. Allow to cool. When mixture is no longer sticky to the touch, cut into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Rice Krispie Treats
raw_recipe.description: Peanut butter Rice Krispies treats without marshmallows combine everyone's favorite cereal snack with peanut butter for a perfect after school treat.
raw_recipe.name: Peanut Butter Rice Krispie Treats

review.reviewBody:
Turned out Perfect, a great alternative to rice crispy treats for people who dont eat gelatin!
I also added in chocolate chips while mixing the peanut butter with the cereal. The chips melted in just enough to make a pretty swirl pattern when spreading it into the pan.

I have been eating these cookies since I was a little girl. They are a family tradition! We mix the sugar and corn syrup and cook until clear. Remove from heat and add peanut butter until fully mixed. Finally fold in cereal. Use wax paper to press into the corners of pan. Melt equal parts of semi sweet and butterscotch chips and spread on top. Let completely cool then cut into one inch pieces. Oh....we call them Kris Kringle's.

These have been in my family since I was very little (over 50 years) We use same recipe, except on top you melt 6 oz of chocolate chips and butterscotch chips together and spread on top and then add sprinkles (I always make them for Christmas, they look so pretty with the red and green sprinkles).

I just made these and they are amazing, I did add an additional half cup of peanut butter and a half cup of Hersheys milk chocolate morsels. I am so glad I did because they probably would have been crumbly and dry if I did not. Great and easy recipe, thanks!!

YUM! I'm a huge peanut butter fan so I added in an extra 1/4 cup of PB. I topped it off with 1/4 cup of peanut butter chips and about 1/2 cup of chocolate chips after they came out of the oven. They had a hard time sticking onto the top so I ended up smoothing it out w/ a spatula.
Only had dark corn syrup on hand. The molasses added a great flavor. Topped with melted semi sweet chips. So good.

I always like to follow a new recipe,as written, the first time I make it and then, if needed, adjust to our liking if I make it again. My husband and I enjoyed this recipe but I personally found it too sweet. I just made it again but this time tweaked it a little. I cut the white sugar in half and doubled the peanut butter. We both enjoyed it more with the stronger peanut butter flavor .
I used to make this when I was a little girl except I used brown sugar. I'm 70 now and still make it!!
I didn't make any changes. It's a little on the sweet side - thus the four stars, but really yummy. Update: I definitely prefer these made with half the sugar.

I've been making peanut butter rice crispies for 30 years. Trust me when I tell you that if you add granulated sugar, it'll harden and be tough. ALSO - this recipe tells you NOTHING about what temp to heat the ingredients to. Do your research. If you heat corn syrup into the 200° range, it will remain gooey when it cools.... but if you mess up....and heat it to 280° and higher... it will become concrete when it cools. This recipe needs nothing but peanut butter, a few pats of butter, and corn syrup (heated to no more than 200-210°. Mix in your rice crispies and pour.
Loved it. I added 1/4 cup of Irish Cream to the melting marshmallows to great success. Highly recommend.

My family loves these peanut butter rice krispie treats. I can't get by with making only one dish, I have to make one for each of my grown grandchildren to take to their homes. At Christmas, this was one of the first dishes to disappear from the table.

I have used this recipe for years and first learned it in home ec class. My family demolishes them when I make it. For anyone needing it: use the butter to grease the 9x13x2 pan. You can also use cooking spray or parchment paper for it. Heat the peanut butter, corn syrup, and sugar in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring until combined and liquidy. The mixture will be slightly grainy. That's ok. Pour it into a large bowl with 6 cups of crisp rice dry cereal, stir well to combine. Dump into greased 9x13 pan, cool, then cut. It is easier to cut these when still slightly warm.
My friends and family are all hooked on this one LOL!

I used cocoa rice crispies and a little coconut flavoring. They were great. I should have cut them sooner than I did. Put them in a gallon Ziploc bag and left them in the fridge for a month. Still tasted great. A A friend suggested I add some instant coffee for flavoring. Will try that soon.
Loved it taste really good if you add marshmallow wiped cream
I also put a coating of chocolate on top of them. These are probably my favorite treat.
Quick and easy, just the way I like it!
I prefer cocoa Krispies for this recipe!❤️
